text: Meanwhile, in the oval flower bed, the snail, whose shell had been stained red, blue, and yellow by the light, now began to labor slowly over the crumbs of loose earth. <break time="0.8s" /> It appeared to have a definite goal in front of it, but before it lay vast obstacles, brown cliffs with deep green lakes in the hollows, flat trees like blades, and round boulders of gray stone. <break time="0.8s" /> Before it had decided whether to circumvent the arched tent of a dead leaf or to breast it, there came past the bed the feet of other human beings, belonging to two men walking side by side. <break time="0.8s" /> The younger of the two, William, wore an expression of perhaps unnatural calm, while the elder walked with an uneven step, jerking his hand forward and throwing up his head abruptly as he spoke. <break time="0.8s" /> He was talking almost without pause about spirits, insisting that heaven had been known to the ancients as Thessaly and that now, with the war, the spirit matter was rolling between the hills like thunder. <break time="0.8s" /> He then explained a little machine through which widows could talk with their dead husbands, but suddenly he caught sight of a womans dark dress in the distance and hurried toward her, muttering excitedly. <break time="0.8s" /> William caught him by the sleeve and touched a flower with the tip of his walking stick, and the confused old man bent his ear to it and seemed to answer a voice speaking from it. <break time="0.8s" /> He began talking about the forests of Uruguay, which he had visited hundreds of years ago with the most beautiful young woman in Europe, and he murmured of nightingales, sea beaches, and mermaids, while William led him patiently on.
